answer.evidence: The tuft is a fan of vertical blades. The silhouette widens from 2 px at row 1 to 14 px at row 11. The lightest pixels are at the blade tips (rows 1-2). Only the blades are seen in elevation, with no horizontal surface. The object is organic ground decor, so the lack of a top surface is expected for a plant, but it still reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a very small tuft, about 10x12 px, so it is smaller than one tile and the per-tile facts read 0. I judged it by eye. Those have layered clumps, several greens, and tinted dark-green shading. The candidate's blades are thin and spiky with little clump structure and no per-blade highlight variety. The outline is not near-neutral (0% neutral edge pixels) and leans dark green, but it is only a thin dark edge with no inner shading, so it reads as a simple sticker. A tall grass tuft can be simple, but it would need 4-5 greens with blade-by-blade highlights to match Beodeul's richness.
